clue.text: Watchful to poor delivery, definitely not out

parts.note: in cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, a poor delivery that costs a run
someone awake is certainly not out cold or asleep

explanation.surface: A batter stays alert to a bad ball and is plainly still in.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface makes 'not out' look like a batting score; here it means not unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fully alert and vigilant is the idiomatic sense of the phrase, a close synonym for watchful.

clue.text: Crank destroys half of cathedral

indicators.note: the cathedral's name loses half its letters, here its second half

parts.note: Winchester Cathedral, in Hampshire, is one of England's great cathedrals

explanation.surface: An eccentric wrecks part of a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crank' suggests an eccentric person; it means the handle-turned device.
explanation.definitionFit: A winch is a hoisting drum turned by a handle, and as a verb crank means to wind or hoist with one.

clue.text: Mother in favour of curbing parking, naturally, that may surround the house

indicators.note: the mother and favour words hold the parking letter in check between them

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
pro means for or in favour of
of course means naturally

explanation.surface: A mother keen on restricting parking might naturally want something round her home.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp-proof course is a waterproof layer laid in the walls just above ground, running round the whole building.

clue.text: Hail storms that are of great concern to cricketers

definitions.text: that are of great concern to cricketers

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail
rages, as a storm or angry person does

explanation.surface: Hailstorms worry cricketers because they stop play.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests weather spoiling a match; the answer is the statistics players watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Batting and bowling averages are the figures by which cricketers' performances are judged.

clue.text: Part and all of circle made taking a bow

parts.note: an arc is part of a circle
the letter O is a whole circle

explanation.surface: A performer goes round a full circle while bowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' suggests a bow to an audience; it is the violinist's bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Arco is the musical direction telling string players to play with the bow again after plucking.

clue.text: One uncle came round, trying to promote unity

indicators.note: the letters are turned round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An uncle came round to make peace in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecumenical describes efforts to bring the different Christian churches together in one fellowship.

clue.text: Mask: guest drops it

indicators.note: the guest word lets go of the letters of it, so they are taken out

parts.note: a visitor is a guest
taken as written

explanation.surface: At a masked party, a guest lets their disguise fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is the movable front of a helmet or a shield for the face, a kind of mask.

clue.text: Old theatre mounting rubbish, a success

parts.note: the Old Vic is a London theatre, so 'old' plus 'theatre' gives Vic

indicators.note: in a down clue the rubbish word climbs, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: A theatre puts on a poor show which turns out to be a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Vic is a famous London theatre; the 'Old' in its name is used up by the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor is one who wins, so a successful person in a contest.

clue.text: Some cut, it is suggested, to make skimpy garment

definitions.meaning: some styles of this beachwear are cut high or low in a suggestive, revealing way
trimming the cloth back is what turns ordinary beachwear into a skimpy one

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the garment: some versions are cut suggestively, which is what makes them skimpy. 'Suggested' plays on suggestive, meaning risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece or two-piece outfit worn for bathing is often cut revealingly, so it can be a skimpy item of clothing.

clue.text: Looking back in admiration to opponent I whipped

parts.note: regard is esteem or admiration

indicators.note: whipped means snatched away, so the I is taken from the opponent word

parts.note: an anti is someone against something
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gazes back admiringly at a beaten opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Regardant is a heraldic term for an animal shown with its head turned to look behind it.

clue.text: Processing some people taking cereal?

parts.note: a number of people is some people
eating crisp breakfast cereal is crunching it

explanation.surface: A group of people file along while eating their breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Processing' suggests walking in a procession; it means handling data.
explanation.definitionFit: Number-crunching is informal for doing large amounts of calculation, the processing of figures by computer.

clue.text: Group of Death's scrapped with passion from the start

indicators.note: the word death is broken up and its letters rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: read as 'Death is', so the word death is what gets scrapped

indicators.note: only the opening letter of passion is wanted here

parts.note: supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: A football 'group of death' is abandoned with great feeling from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of death' is the football term for the hardest group in a tournament draw, but the definition is just 'Group'.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptad is a set of seven things, so it is a particular kind of group.

clue.text: Course on religion by old Luther, for one

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject that teaches religion
former means of an earlier time, old

explanation.surface: Martin Luther is pictured as an old figure on a theology course.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther led the Protestant Reformation, so he is the prime example of a church reformer.

clue.text: Piece of music involved Sinatra, too

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so these letters are mixed together anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra also took part in a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio sonata is a baroque composition for two melody instruments and a bass line.

clue.text: With difficulty, old woman eats one chewy sort of food

parts.note: to be in a hole is to be in difficulty

indicators.note: the old woman word takes the one inside it, as if eating it

parts.note: gran, short for grandmother, is an old woman

explanation.surface: An elderly woman struggles to get through something hard to chew.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholegrain bread and cereals keep the bran and germ of the grain, giving a chewier texture than refined food.

clue.text: Capricious Manx cat not acceptable in stage show

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the cat word loses its last letter

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip, so cat means whip

indicators.note: U means upper-class and acceptable, so the show word is made non-U by losing it

parts.note: a musical is a stage show

explanation.surface: A tailless cat proves unwelcome in a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' for upper-class or socially acceptable is a crossword convention, so 'not acceptable' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical means acting on sudden fancies, as unpredictable as a capricious person.

clue.text: Tongue almost swallowed by Puss?
From small stool, cheers soldiers entering boxing match

parts.note: ta is British for thanks

indicators.note: the soldiers go into the boxing match word

parts.note: a bout is a boxing contest
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers cheer as they climb into the ring from a corner stool.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabouret is a low seat without a back or arms, a stool.

clue.text: Problematic moment, facing execution

indicators.note: execution here means beheading, so the moment word loses its first letter

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment

explanation.surface: A tricky moment comes just before someone is put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: Beheading is the crossword sense of execution: the head of the word is cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or dodgy, so a problematic situation is an iffy one.

clue.text: Meeting prince, perhaps, not an Englishman

parts.note: a prince is one example of a royal
a Scot is a Briton who is not English, here with the article: a Scot

explanation.surface: Someone meets a prince and turns out not to be English.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is a June race meeting at Ascot racecourse in Berkshire, attended by the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing a meeting is a series of races held at one course over a day or days.

clue.text: Bright sort of weather breaking through

indicators.note: the weather word breaks into the middle of the through word

parts.note: by means through or via
rain is one sort of weather

explanation.surface: Sunny weather breaks through the clouds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright' looks like weather; it means clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainy means clever, as bright does of a person.

clue.text: Play area in commercial premises

parts.note: a play is a show
room is space or area

explanation.surface: A children's play area sits inside a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A showroom is a shop or space where goods such as cars or furniture are displayed for sale.

clue.text: Non-European doctor excellent for small growth

indicators.note: the doctor word is left without its letter for European

parts.note: Bones is slang for a doctor, as with Dr McCoy in Star Trek
A1, read as letters, means first-class

explanation.surface: An Asian doctor's skill is praised in treating a little lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' suggests a medical lump next to 'doctor'; it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a tree kept deliberately miniature by pruning, a small plant growth.

clue.text: An extra page a day for teachers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an extra page or section inserted into a book or magazine
second meaning: an ... day, a school day set aside for staff training

explanation.walkthrough: In British schools an INSET day (in-service education and training) is a day when pupils stay home and teachers are trained.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a leaf inserted into a publication and the British name for a staff training day.

clue.text: Eggs left in ground

parts.note: ova are egg cells

explanation.surface: Eggs are left buried in the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' suggests soil; it is a sports ground. The Oval is a London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval in Kennington is a famous Test cricket venue, an example of a sports ground.

clue.text: Having arrived, lunatics damaged important goods

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are knocked out of shape and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Madmen turn up and wreck valuable merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goods' looks like merchandise, but it means moral goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The cardinal virtues, prudence, justice, temperance and fortitude, are the chief moral goods of classical and Christian ethics.

clue.text: Cautious line sounding weird

indicators.note: the weird word is spoken, giving its sound but a different spelling

parts.note: eerie means strange and unsettling

explanation.surface: A wary remark has an odd ring to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leery means wary or suspicious, a synonym for cautious.

clue.text: Share in growing concern

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a portion handed out to someone
second meaning: a rented plot of land for growing vegetables

explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing concern' is an idiom for an expanding business; here it is literally where things are grown. An allotment is a small rented plot for growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a portion allocated to someone and a plot of land rented for cultivation.
